title: Sola fide is not bare believing act vs love/hope/repentance—living faith includes them
source_text: XXX. Imo, quum solam fidem justificare dicimus, ne id quidem significamus, solum credendi actum praecise sumptum, prout actibus amoris & spei opponitur, & distinguitur a resipiscentia, sive poenitentia, esse conditionem, quam novum foedus, sive Evangelium postulat, ut peccatorum nostrorum remissionem consequamur, & propter Christum ab iis absolvamur. Nam veniae spes & Dei dilectio, itemque dolor de peccato, & novae vitae propositum, ac uno verbo, actus omnes ad veram & seriam conversionem requisiti, sunt etiam quiddam necessarium & omnino praerequisitum, ut aliquis a Deo in gratiam recipiatur, & ab eo deinceps habeatur pro justificato. Imo fides illa viva & per charitatem operans, quam justificare solam affirmamus, omnia ista includit, & involvit.
pass_a_gloss: Indeed, when we say faith alone justifies, we do not even mean that the bare act of believing precisely taken, as opposed to acts of love and hope and distinguished from repentance, is the condition the new covenant or Gospel requires so that we may obtain remission of our sins and be absolved from them for Christ's sake. For hope of pardon and love of God, likewise sorrow for sin and purpose of new life—and in a word, all acts required for true and serious conversion—are also something necessary and altogether prerequisite for someone to be received by God into grace and thereafter held by him as justified. Indeed that living faith working through charity which alone we affirm justifies includes and involves all these.
pass_b_english: Sola fide is not the bare believing act cut off from love, hope, and repentance.
Living charity-working faith includes conversion's required acts as prerequisite.

lemmas.gloss: the act of believing precisely taken

choices.why: Not excluded from living justifying faith.
